title: A Quranic Verse that Nobody Understood!
normalized_text: a lot of us only touch the quran during ramadan and when we do we fall into a very bad habit of reading with the intention of completing it due to this we don't have time to contemplate the meanings behind the verses we overlook context we do not ask why are these words written in this order and what is going on with the word choice in this verse in this video i'd like to share some thoughts on a specific verse with the intention of getting you my friend to take your time when reading the quran and to realize that the text that you have laying on your shelf collecting dust is magical and very truly our messengers came to abraham with glad tidings they said peace he said peace and soon after he came with a roasted calf but when he saw their hands not reaching towards it he distrusted them and conceived a fear of them they said do not fear we have indeed been sent to the people of lot and his wife was standing by so she laughed and we gave her glad tidings of isaac and after isaac jacob one more time and his wife was standing by so she laughed and we gave her glad tidings of isaac and after isaac jacob most of us are not aware of the eloquence within this verse it seems pretty straightforward doesn't seem like there's much to it however the word play is obvious to those that are familiar with hebrew the name isaac or itzhak literally means he laughs in other words the wife abraham laughed and therefore she was blessed with a son named he laughs then after isaac jacob or yakov which literally means to follow an intricate form of wordplay that is clearly intentional with a clear understanding of the hebrew language as well as a familiarity with genesis 18. and he said i will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life and lo sarah thy wife shall have a son and sarah heard it in the tent door which was behind him now abraham and sarah were old and well stricken in age and it ceased to be with sarah after the manner of women therefore sarah laughed within herself saying after i am waxed old shall i have pleasure my lord being old also interestingly there's no mentioning of jacob in the verses here which proves that the word play isn't based on some sort of plagiarism but it is due to knowledge of hebrew here's where even gets more interesting how did classical first century muslims understand these verses we do find attributions to major classical exegetes like in mujahid in which they state that vahiket meaning laughed actually meant menstruated in other words sarah menstruated and then was given the good news about her having isaac now this understanding seems to have come from a classical line of poetry in which the word the vlajeket was used by an anonymous classical poet to mean menstruated however others like benue who was from a jewish background took the verse literally which is natural since he was familiar with genesis and ibn putaba in the third century points out that this literal understanding is supported by the torah in other words due to his understanding of hebrew took the verse literally since he was aware of the word play in the verse interestingly we do not find classical exegetes going into the meaning of isaac or jacob apparently since they weren't aware of the significance of their names within the context of the verse we do not find them refuting the biblical accounts either or rejecting them what can we conclude from this well we can conclude that the author of the quran had access to information that classical exegetes did not have access to the claim that muhammad peace be upon him copied from the bible conflicts with information that we would expect to find in classical works of tafsir the claim that this information was available to society also is not in line with what we would expect to find in those works and this is just one verse of many in which the quran plays on words makes puns and engages with scriptures in a different language in a manner that wasn't even appreciated by the scholars of first century arabia well with the exception of those from jewish background that wholeheartedly accept islam and ended up converting so once again guys don't read the quran with the intention of finishing the chapter read it knowing that there are gems waiting for you to uncover lessons to be learned and a gift from your creator that is waiting to be appreciated
